# Jubilees Chapter 45 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Jacob in Egypt; Jacob's death and burial at Machpelah

---

**45:1** And Jacob lived in Egypt seventeen years. And all the days of his life were one hundred and forty-seven years.

**45:2** And Jacob called all his sons and said to them: "I am dying. I am gathering to my people. Bury me with my fathers."

**45:3** And he commanded them with regard to the burying of his body, as Isaac had commanded him, and as Abraham had commanded Isaac. And he bowed upon the head of his bed and died.

**45:4** And Joseph fell upon the face of his father and wept and kissed him.

**45:5** And Joseph commanded his servants the physicians to embalm his father. And they embalmed Israel.

**45:6** And forty days were fulfilled for him — for so many days are fulfilled for the embalmed. And the Egyptians mourned for Israel seventy days.

**45:7** And all the house of Jacob mourned for him. And when the days of mourning were fulfilled, Joseph said to Pharaoh: "If I have found favor in thine eyes, speak, I pray thee, in the ears of Pharaoh."

**45:8** And Pharaoh said: "Go up and bury thy father as he commanded thee." And Joseph went up to bury his father.

**45:9** And all the elders of Egypt and all the great men of Pharaoh's house went up with him. And all his brothers went with him. And Joseph took with him from Goshen all his father's household — only their small children and their flocks and their herds they left in Goshen.

**45:10** And there went up with him chariots and horsemen — a very great company. And they came to Atad on the other side of Jordan, and they mourned there a great and heavy mourning for seven days.

**45:11** And they made a lamentation for Israel at Atad, and the Canaanites who dwelt in the land saw the mourning at Atad and said: "This is a heavy mourning to the Egyptians." Therefore its name was called Abel Mizraim — "meadow of Egypt" — which is beyond Jordan.

**45:12** And the sons of Israel carried their father and buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the Hittite, over against Mamre. And they returned to Egypt, they and all those with them.

**45:13** And Joseph mourned for his father seven days, and all his brothers mourned with him. And the mourning of his father was very great.

---

*EMET notes: The death, embalming, and burial of Jacob (vv.1-13) follows Genesis 47:28-50:14 in compressed form. The Jubilees account adds the detail that Jacob bowed his head and died (v.3) — a Ge'ez rendering of the Genesis "gathered up his feet" that is interpreted as a dying gesture of worship. Abel Mizraim etymology (v.11) follows Genesis 50:11.*
